title.zh: 卷141 志一百十六 兵十二 马政
title.raw: 卷141 志一百十六 兵十二 马政

sentences.zh: 志一百十六

translations.literal: Treatise one hundred sixteen.
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 116

sentences.zh: 兵十二

translations.literal: Military twelve.
translations.idiomatic: Military 12

sentences.zh: 馬政

translations.literal: Horse administration.
translations.idiomatic: Horse Administration

sentences.zh: 清初沿明制，設御馬監，康熙間，改為上駟院，掌御馬，以備上乘。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Qing, following the Ming system, the Imperial Horse Bureau was established; during the Kangxi reign it was changed to the Upper Stud Court, which managed imperial horses to supply mounts for riding.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qing dynasty the court followed the Ming model and established the Imperial Horse Bureau; under Kangxi this was reorganized as the Upper Stud Court, charged with imperial horses for the emperor's riding.

sentences.zh: 畜以備御者，曰內馬；

translations.literal: Horses kept for imperial use were called inner horses;
translations.idiomatic: Horses raised for the emperor's use were termed inner horses;

sentences.zh: 供儀仗者，曰仗馬。

translations.literal: those supplied for ceremonial guard were called ceremonial horses.
translations.idiomatic: those provided for ceremonial escort were called ceremonial horses.

sentences.zh: 御馬選入，以印烙之。

translations.literal: When imperial horses were selected and brought in, they were branded with a seal.
translations.idiomatic: Selected imperial horses were admitted and branded with an official mark.

sentences.zh: 設蒙古馬醫官療馬病。

translations.literal: Mongol horse doctors were appointed to treat equine illness.
translations.idiomatic: Mongol veterinary officers were appointed to treat sick horses.

sentences.zh: 上巡幸及行圍，扈從官弁，各給官馬。

translations.literal: When the emperor toured or went on hunting expeditions, each officer in the entourage was issued a government horse.
translations.idiomatic: On imperial tours and hunting expeditions, every officer in the entourage was issued a government mount.

sentences.zh: 以副都統或侍衛為放馬大臣，主其事。

translations.literal: A deputy lieutenant-general or an imperial bodyguard served as Horse Distribution Minister and directed the matter.
translations.idiomatic: A deputy lieutenant-general or imperial guardsman was appointed Horse Distribution Minister to oversee the arrangements.

sentences.zh: 上謁祖陵，需馬二萬三千餘匹，東西陵需馬四千三百餘匹，悉取察哈爾牧廠馬應之。

translations.literal: When the emperor paid homage at the ancestral tombs, more than twenty-three thousand horses were required; for the Eastern and Western Tombs more than four thousand three hundred were needed—all supplied from Chahar stud farms.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial visits to the ancestral mausoleums required over twenty-three thousand horses, and visits to the Eastern and Western Tombs over four thousand three hundred—all drawn from Chahar stud farms.

sentences.zh: 迨乾隆時，每扈從用馬匹輒二萬餘。

translations.literal: By the Qianlong period, each entourage routinely used more than twenty thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: By the Qianlong reign, each imperial entourage routinely required more than twenty thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶中，物力漸耗，停木蘭秋獮。

translations.literal: During the Jiaqing reign material resources gradually dwindled, and the Mulan autumn hunt was suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jiaqing, as resources grew scarce, the Mulan autumn hunt was discontinued.

sentences.zh: 十二年，減額馬之半。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, allotted horses were cut by half.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of his reign, the allotted number of horses was reduced by half.

sentences.zh: 道光九年，如盛京謁陵，額馬視乾隆時，約略相等，計取給廠馬暨各盟長所進，蓋二萬六千餘匹雲。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Daoguang, when proceeding to Mukden to worship at the tombs, the allotted horses were roughly equal to the Qianlong period; counting stud-farm horses and those presented by league chiefs, the total came to more than twenty-six thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 9, when the emperor went to Mukden to worship at the tombs, the allotted horses were roughly on par with the Qianlong era; between stud-farm issues and presentations from league chiefs, the total exceeded twenty-six thousand.

sentences.zh: 順治十五年定軍馬，親王出征，馬四百匹，郡王三百，貝勒二百，貝子百五十，鎮國公百匹，輔國公八十，不入八分鎮國公七十，輔國公六十五，將軍八十，副將軍七十，護軍統領、前鋒統領、副都統皆六十，其下各有差，最少者護軍、領催各六匹。

translations.literal: In Shunzhi 15 military horse quotas were fixed: a prince of the first rank on campaign received four hundred horses, a prince of the second rank three hundred, a beile two hundred, a beizi one hundred fifty, a defender duke of the state one hundred, a bulwark duke of the state eighty, a defender duke of the state not in the Eight Privileges seventy, a bulwark duke of the state sixty-five, a general eighty, a deputy general seventy, and commanders of the Vanguard, Forward, and deputy lieutenant-generals sixty each, with graded reductions below; the minimum was six horses each for guardsmen and squad leaders.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 15 the court fixed military horse allotments: a first-rank prince on campaign received four hundred horses, a second-rank prince three hundred, a beile two hundred, a beizi one hundred fifty, a defender duke of the state one hundred, a bulwark duke eighty, a defender duke outside the Eight Privileges seventy, a bulwark duke sixty-five, a general eighty, a deputy general seventy, and commanders of the Vanguard, Forward, and deputy lieutenant-generals sixty each, with lower ranks scaled down to a minimum of six horses for guardsmen and squad leaders.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十五年，敕出徵兵一人馬四匹，四人為伍，一伍主從騎八匹，馱器糧用具亦八匹。

translations.literal: In Kangxi 35 it was ordered that each soldier on campaign have four horses; four men formed a squad, with eight riding horses and eight pack animals for equipment, grain, and gear per squad.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 35 the emperor ordered that each soldier on campaign receive four horses; four men formed a squad, with eight riding mounts and eight pack animals for equipment, grain, and supplies per squad.

sentences.zh: 是歲，征噶爾丹，以兵丁馬瘦，褫兵部尚書索諾和職。

translations.literal: That year, campaigning against Galdan, because the troops' horses were emaciated, Minister of War Suo'nuohe was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: That year, during the campaign against Galdan, the troops' horses were found too thin, and Minister of War Suo'nuohe was stripped of his post.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，覈定軍中職官馬數，大學士、尚書、左都御史十六匹，侍郎以下遞減，經略、大將軍各二十五匹，副將軍以下遞減。

translations.literal: In year 51 the allotted horses for army officers were verified: grand secretaries, ministers, and the left censor-in-chief received sixteen each, vice-ministers and below in descending order, grand coordinators and commanders-in-chief twenty-five each, and deputy commanders-in-chief and below in descending order.
translations.idiomatic: In year 51 the court audited military horse allotments for officers: grand secretaries, ministers, and the left censor-in-chief received sixteen each, with vice-ministers and lower ranks scaled down; grand coordinators and commanders-in-chief received twenty-five each, with deputy commanders-in-chief and below likewise reduced.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十六年，八旗牧官馬二萬七千七百餘匹，以萬匹於都城外牧養，熱河千匹，各庄頭二千匹，餘者分畀直隸標營。

translations.literal: In Qianlong 16 the Eight Banners pastured more than twenty-seven thousand seven hundred government horses; ten thousand were kept outside the capital, one thousand at Rehe, two thousand with various estate managers, and the remainder distributed to Zhili banner garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 16 the Eight Banners pastured over twenty-seven thousand seven hundred government horses: ten thousand outside the capital, one thousand at Rehe, two thousand with estate managers, and the rest allotted to Zhili banner garrisons.

sentences.zh: 圈馬之設，始乾隆二十八年，從都統舒赫德請也。

translations.literal: The establishment of corral horses began in Qianlong 28, following the request of lieutenant-general Shuhede.
translations.idiomatic: Corral horses were first instituted in Qianlong 28 at the request of lieutenant-general Shuhede.

sentences.zh: 滿洲八旗，旗養馬二百匹。

translations.literal: Each banner of the Manchu Eight Banners pastured two hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: Each Manchu banner maintained two hundred corral horses.

sentences.zh: 蒙古八旗，旗百匹。

translations.literal: Each banner of the Mongol Eight Banners, one hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Each Mongol banner maintained one hundred.

sentences.zh: 洎五十九年撤圈，分給各兵拴養。

translations.literal: By year 59 the corrals were abolished and the horses distributed for soldiers to tether and raise individually.
translations.idiomatic: By year 59 the corrals were abolished and the horses distributed for individual tethering by soldiers.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十二年，諭成親王永星議復圈馬，大學士戴衢亨等會議，立章程十條，圈馬仍舊。

translations.literal: In Jiaqing 12 the emperor ordered Prince Cheng Yongxing to deliberate on restoring corral horses; Grand Secretary Dai Quheng and others met in conference, drew up ten articles of regulation, and corral horses were maintained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 12 the emperor directed Prince Cheng Yongxing to consider restoring corral horses; Grand Secretary Dai Quheng and others convened, drafted ten regulations, and corral horses were kept as before.

sentences.zh: 道光末，軍興遂廢，後亦不復籌矣。

translations.literal: At the end of Daoguang, with warfare arising, the system was abandoned and never revived.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of Daoguang, with war underway, the system was abandoned and never restored.

sentences.zh: 同治元年諭曰：「馬政廢弛，積弊已深，以致軍馬罷瘠。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi an edict stated: 'Horse administration has fallen into neglect; long-standing abuses run deep, so that army horses are worn and thin.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 1 an edict declared: 'Horse administration has lapsed; abuses have accumulated so deeply that army horses are exhausted and emaciated.

sentences.zh: 牧廠大臣等應妥實整頓，差功罪以挽頹風，著為令。

translations.literal: Ministers of stud farms and the like should thoroughly rectify matters, distinguishing merit and fault to reverse the decline, and this is hereby made regulation.'
translations.idiomatic: Stud-farm superintendents and the like must undertake a thorough overhaul, rewarding merit and punishing fault to reverse the decline—let this be established as law.'

sentences.zh: 」溯自世祖入關，迄於康、乾之際，盛京、吉林、黑龍江、直隸、江南、浙江、廣東、福建、湖北、四川、陝、甘、山東、山西諸省設駐防滿洲營，馬凡十萬六千四百餘匹，惟福建水師駐防僅數十匹。

translations.literal: Looking back from the Shizu emperor's entry into China to the Kangxi and Qianlong periods, garrison Manchu camps were established in Shengjing, Jilin, Heilongjiang, Zhili, Jiangnan, Zhejiang, Guangdong, Fujian, Hubei, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Gansu, Shandong, and Shanxi, with a total of more than one hundred six thousand four hundred horses; only the Fujian naval garrison had a few dozen.
translations.idiomatic: From the Shunzhi emperor's entry into China through the Kangxi and Qianlong eras, Manchu garrisons were posted across Shengjing, Jilin, Heilongjiang, Zhili, Jiangnan, Zhejiang, Guangdong, Fujian, Hubei, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Gansu, Shandong, and Shanxi, totaling over one hundred six thousand four hundred horses—only the Fujian naval garrison held a few dozen.

sentences.zh: 乾隆季年，定西藏兵制，前藏供差營馬六十匹，後藏二十匹，舊塘四十三，共塘馬二百二十匹，新設番塘二十四，共番馬九十八匹。

translations.literal: In the late Qianlong period Tibet's military establishment was fixed: Front Tibet had sixty service horses, Rear Tibet twenty, forty-three old courier stations totaling two hundred twenty station horses, and twenty-four newly established native courier stations with ninety-eight native horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Qianlong period the Tibet garrison was fixed: Front Tibet received sixty service horses, Rear Tibet twenty; forty-three established courier stations totaled two hundred twenty station horses, and twenty-four newly established native stations ninety-eight native horses.

sentences.zh: 黑龍江兵向無額馬，道光十六年，從哈豐阿請，始設置之。

translations.literal: Heilongjiang troops had never had allotted horses; in Daoguang 16, following Hafeng'a's request, allotments were first established.
translations.idiomatic: Heilongjiang troops had never held allotted horses; in Daoguang 16, at Hafeng'a's request, allotments were first instituted.

sentences.zh: 天聰時，征服察哈爾，其地宜牧，馬蕃息。

translations.literal: In the Tiancong period Chahar was conquered; the land was suited to pasturage and horses multiplied.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tiancong the court conquered Chahar; the region was ideal for grazing and horses multiplied abundantly.

sentences.zh: 順治初，大庫口外設種馬廠，隸兵部。

translations.literal: Early in Shunzhi a breeding stud was set up outside Daku Pass, subordinate to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shunzhi a breeding stud was established beyond Daku Pass under the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 康熙九年，改牧廠屬太僕寺，分左翼右翼二廠，均在口外。

translations.literal: In Kangxi 9 stud farms were transferred to the Court of the Imperial Stud, divided into left- and right-wing farms, both beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 9 stud farms were placed under the Court of the Imperial Stud and divided into left- and right-wing establishments, both beyond the frontier passes.

sentences.zh: 是時，大凌河設牧廠一，邊牆設廠二，曰商都達布遜諾爾，曰達里岡愛，隸上駟院。

translations.literal: At that time one stud was set up on the Daling River and two along the border wall, called Shangdu Dabuxunuo'er and Daligang'ai, subordinate to the Upper Stud Court.
translations.idiomatic: At that time one stud was established on the Daling River and two along the border wall—Shangdu Dabuxunuo'er and Daligang'ai—under the Upper Stud Court.

sentences.zh: 尋分設牧廠五，曰大凌河牧群馬營，曰養息牧哈達牧群馬營，曰養息所邊外蘇魯克牧牛羊群，及黑牛群牧營，曰養息牧邊外牧群牛營，並在盛京境。

translations.literal: Soon five stud farms were separately established: the Daling River Horse Herd Camp, the Yangxi Pasture Hada Horse Herd Camp, the Yangxi Office's Surok herds of cattle and sheep beyond the border, and the Black Cattle Herd Camp, and the Yangxi Pasture herds of cattle beyond the border—all within Shengjing territory.
translations.idiomatic: Five stud farms were soon added: the Daling River Horse Herd Camp, the Yangxi Pasture Hada Horse Herd Camp, the Yangxi Office's Surok cattle-and-sheep herds beyond the border, the Black Cattle Herd Camp, and the Yangxi Pasture cattle herds beyond the border—all in Shengjing territory.

sentences.zh: 凡馬牡曰兒，牝曰果，不及三歲曰駒，及壯擇割其牡曰騸。

translations.literal: For horses, males were called er, females guo, those under three years foals, and when mature selected stallions were gelded and called shan.
translations.idiomatic: Stallions were termed er, mares guo, horses under three years foals, and selected mature stallions were gelded as shan.

sentences.zh: 別其騍騸以為群，率騍馬五配兒馬一，群無過四百匹。

translations.literal: Mares and geldings were separated into herds; generally five mares were matched to one stallion, and no herd exceeded four hundred head.
translations.idiomatic: Mares and geldings were grouped separately; typically five mares were assigned to one stallion, and no herd exceeded four hundred head.

sentences.zh: 騍馬及羊三年一平群，牛六年，騍馬群三歲以息補耗，三馬而取一駒，騸馬群歲耗其十一。

translations.literal: Mare herds and sheep were balanced every three years, cattle every six; mare herds replenished losses with increase every three years, taking one foal per three mares, and gelding herds lost one in eleven annually.
translations.idiomatic: Mare herds and sheep were rebalanced every three years, cattle every six; mare herds replenished losses every three years at a rate of one foal per three mares, while gelding herds sustained an annual loss of one in eleven.

sentences.zh: 置牧長、牧副、牧丁任其事，轄以協領、翼長、總管，官兵皆察哈爾、蒙古人充之。

translations.literal: Head herdsmen, deputy herdsmen, and herd attendants were appointed to manage affairs, supervised by assistant commandants, wing commanders, and superintendents; officers and men were all Chahar and Mongols.
translations.idiomatic: Head herdsmen, deputies, and attendants managed the herds under assistant commandants, wing commanders, and superintendents; all officers and men were drawn from Chahar and Mongol ranks.

sentences.zh: 飼秣所需木槽鏇钁鑹杓，每群各二，五年一給之。

translations.literal: Feeding gear—wooden troughs, augers, hoes, spades, and ladles—two sets per herd, were issued every five years.
translations.idiomatic: Feeding equipment—wooden troughs, augers, hoes, spades, and ladles—two sets per herd, was issued every five years.

sentences.zh: 總管三年番代。

translations.literal: Superintendents rotated every three years.
translations.idiomatic: Superintendents served three-year rotations.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，定牧群牲畜歲終彙報增減數目，視其贏絀，以第賞罰。

translations.literal: In year 24 it was fixed that at year's end herds reported increases and decreases; according to surplus or deficit, rewards and punishments were graded.
translations.idiomatic: In year 24 the court required annual year-end reports on herd increases and decreases, with rewards and punishments graded according to surplus or deficit.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，令八旗豢馬，春夏驅赴察哈爾牧放，曰出青，秋冬迴圈，曰回青。

translations.literal: In year 26 the Eight Banners' kept horses were ordered driven to Chahar for summer and spring pasture, called 'going out to green,' and returned to the corrals in autumn and winter, called 'returning to green.'
translations.idiomatic: In year 26 Banner horses were driven to Chahar for spring and summer grazing—'going out to green'—and returned to the corrals in autumn and winter—'returning to green.'

sentences.zh: 四十四年，將軍楊福請市馬給兵丁，上不許，諭曰：「朝廷屢以太僕寺廠馬並茶馬給各兵丁，故無賠馬之苦。

translations.literal: In year 44 General Yang Fu requested to purchase horses for the troops; the emperor did not permit it and instructed: 'The court has repeatedly issued Court of the Imperial Stud farm horses and tea-horse horses to each soldier, so there is no hardship of compensating for horses.
translations.idiomatic: In year 44 General Yang Fu asked to buy horses for the troops; the emperor refused, stating: 'The court has repeatedly issued stud-farm and tea-horse mounts to the troops, sparing them the burden of compensation.

sentences.zh: 歷觀宋、明議馬政，皆無善策。

translations.literal: Reviewing Song and Ming discussions of horse policy, none had good measures.
translations.idiomatic: A review of Song and Ming horse policy shows that none devised a sound solution.

sentences.zh: 牧馬惟口外最善，水草肥美，不糜餉而孳生甚多。

translations.literal: Pasturing horses beyond the passes alone is best; water and grass are rich, without exhausting provisions yet producing abundantly.
translations.idiomatic: Pasturage beyond the passes alone is optimal: water and forage are rich, costs no grain ration, yet herds multiply abundantly.

sentences.zh: 如驅入內地牧之，即日費萬金不足矣。

translations.literal: If driven to pasture within the interior, ten thousand in gold per day would not suffice.'
translations.idiomatic: Drive them to pasture inside China proper, and ten thousand taels a day would not cover the cost.'

sentences.zh: 」雍正三年，定在廠馬以四萬匹為率。

translations.literal: In Yongzheng 3 the stud-farm quota was fixed at forty thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 3 the stud-farm quota was fixed at forty thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 至乾隆五年，足額外，溢七千餘匹。

translations.literal: By Qianlong 5, beyond filling the quota, there was a surplus of more than seven thousand.
translations.idiomatic: By Qianlong 5 the herds exceeded the quota by more than seven thousand head.

sentences.zh: 兩翼牧廠，共騍馬百六十群，騸馬十六群，令分在兩翼廠牧放。

translations.literal: The two-wing stud farms had altogether one hundred sixty mare herds and sixteen gelding herds, ordered to pasture separately at the two-wing farms.
translations.idiomatic: The two-wing stud farms maintained one hundred sixty mare herds and sixteen gelding herds, pastured separately at each wing.

sentences.zh: 八年，敕牧界毋許侵越。

translations.literal: In year 8 it was ordered that pasture boundaries must not be encroached upon.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 the emperor forbade encroachment on pasture boundaries.

sentences.zh: 先是甘、涼、肅三州及西寧各設馬廠，分五群，群儲牝馬二百匹，牡四十。

translations.literal: Earlier, Gansu, Liangzhou, Suzhou, and Xining each established horse farms divided into five herds, each storing two hundred mares and forty stallions.
translations.idiomatic: Previously horse farms were established in Ganzhou, Liangzhou, Suzhou, and Xining, each divided into five herds of two hundred mares and forty stallions.

sentences.zh: 尋改甘州廠屬巴里坤。

translations.literal: Soon the Ganzhou farm was transferred to Barkul.
translations.idiomatic: The Ganzhou farm was soon reassigned to Barkul.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，伊犁設孳生馬駝廠，畀錫伯、察哈爾、索倫、厄魯特四營牧之。

translations.literal: In year 25 a breeding farm for horses and camels was set up in Ili, entrusted to the Xibe, Chahar, Solon, and Oirat four camps for pasturing.
translations.idiomatic: In year 25 a breeding farm for horses and camels was established in Ili, pastured by the Xibe, Chahar, Solon, and Oirat camps.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，定牧廠官屬所需馬，視內地驛傳例，按官品給之，不得逾額。

translations.literal: In year 32 horses required by stud-farm officials were fixed according to the interior courier-post precedent, issued by rank without exceeding quota.
translations.idiomatic: In year 32 mounts for stud-farm officials were allotted by rank following interior courier-post precedent, without exceeding quota.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶中，從都統慶溥言，撤回厄魯特人牧廠。

translations.literal: During Jiaqing, following lieutenant-general Qing Pu's statement, Oirat pasture of the stud farm was withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: During Jiaqing, at lieutenant-general Qing Pu's recommendation, Oirat herders were withdrawn from the stud farms.

sentences.zh: 初，富俊建言，撤大凌河牧廠，分歸東三省，仁宗嚴諭斥之。

translations.literal: Earlier Fu Jun proposed abolishing the Daling River stud and dividing it among the Three Eastern Provinces; the Jiaqing emperor sternly rebuked this.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Fu Jun proposed abolishing the Daling River stud and reallocating its herds to the Three Eastern Provinces; the Jiaqing emperor sharply rebuked the suggestion.

sentences.zh: 迨道光七年，上經杏山東閱馬廠，見河岸馬群壯整。

translations.literal: By Daoguang 7, when the emperor passed Xingshan on an inspection tour of the stud farm, he saw herds along the riverbank strong and well-formed.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 7, passing Xingshan on an inspection of the stud farm, the emperor saw strong, well-formed herds along the riverbank.

sentences.zh: 因諭是間牧廠寬闊，水草蕃滋，馬恃以生息，若輕議裁，則散之甚易，聚之甚難。

translations.literal: He therefore instructed that the pasture here was broad, water and grass abundant, and horses depended on it for breeding; if lightly proposed for reduction, dispersal would be very easy but gathering very difficult.
translations.idiomatic: He observed that these pastures were vast and forage abundant, sustaining the herds' breeding; rash proposals to cut them would scatter the herds easily yet make reassembly exceedingly difficult.

sentences.zh: 再有率為此請者，以違制論。

translations.literal: Whoever again led such a request would be judged for violating regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who again led such a proposal would be prosecuted for violating regulations.

sentences.zh: 咸豐四年，科爾沁親王僧格林沁剿捻，檄取察哈爾戰馬六百匹，不堪乘用，奏聞。

translations.literal: In Xianfeng 4 Prince Senggelinqin of Horqin, suppressing the Nian, requisitioned six hundred Chahar war horses; they were unfit for riding and this was reported.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 4 Prince Senggelinqin of Horqin, campaigning against the Nian rebels, requisitioned six hundred Chahar war horses; found unfit for riding, the matter was reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，嚴諭都統慶昀整頓，蓋馬政漸衰弛矣。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and sternly ordered lieutenant-general Qing Yun to rectify matters—for horse administration was gradually declining.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and sternly ordered lieutenant-general Qing Yun to overhaul the system—horse administration was clearly in decline.

sentences.zh: 光緒九年，太僕寺言兩翼騍馬騸馬一百十四群，並孳生馬五群，駝亦五群，較乾隆時群數大減。

translations.literal: In Guangxu 9 the Court of the Imperial Stud reported one hundred fourteen mare and gelding herds on the two wings, plus five breeding horse herds and five camel herds—a great reduction from Qianlong herd numbers.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 9 the Court of the Imperial Stud reported one hundred fourteen mare and gelding herds on the two wings, plus five breeding horse herds and five camel herds—a sharp decline from Qianlong levels.

sentences.zh: 嗣是穆圖善練兵，至黑龍江求馬無良，愀然曰：「地氣其盡乎！

translations.literal: Thereafter Mutushan trained troops; reaching Heilongjiang he sought horses but found none sound, and said mournfully: 'Has the land's vital force been exhausted!'
translations.idiomatic: Later Mutushan drilled troops; reaching Heilongjiang he found no sound horses and said mournfully: 'Has the region's vital force been exhausted!'

sentences.zh: 」迨於末葉，厲行新法，舊時牧政益廢不講，豈非時勢使然歟？

translations.literal: By the dynasty's end, vigorously implementing new methods, the old pasture administration was increasingly abandoned and neglected—is this not what the times demanded?'
translations.idiomatic: By the dynasty's end, as new reforms were pressed forward, the old pasture system was increasingly abandoned—is this not simply what the times required?'

sentences.zh: 順治初，陝西設洮岷、河州、西寧、庄浪、甘州茶馬司，及開成、安定、廣寧、黑水、清平、萬安、武安七監，歲遣御史一人專理之。

translations.literal: Early in Shunzhi Shaanxi established Tea-Horse offices at Taomin, Hezhou, Xining, Zhuanglang, and Ganzhou, and seven supervisory stations at Kaicheng, Anding, Guangning, Heishui, Qingping, Wan'an, and Wu'an; each year one censor was dispatched to manage them exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shunzhi Shaanxi established Tea-Horse offices at Taomin, Hezhou, Xining, Zhuanglang, and Ganzhou, plus seven supervisory stations at Kaicheng, Anding, Guangning, Heishui, Qingping, Wan'an, and Wu'an; annually one censor was dispatched to oversee them.

sentences.zh: 七年，喀爾喀、額魯特來市馬，諭令自章京監察之販客及賈人，與不系披甲者，概不許購，違者鞭一百，馬入官。

translations.literal: In year 7 Khalkha and Oirat came to trade horses; it was ordered that from clerks supervising down to peddlers and merchants, and those not in armor, none were permitted to purchase; violators received one hundred lashes and horses were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 Khalkha and Oirat came to trade horses; the court ruled that supervising clerks, peddlers, merchants, and anyone not in military service were forbidden to buy—violators received one hundred lashes and horses were confiscated.

sentences.zh: 蒙古攜馬來京，不許商販私買，胥役私購者罪之。

translations.literal: When Mongols brought horses to the capital, merchants were not permitted to buy privately; clerks and runners who purchased privately were punished.
translations.idiomatic: When Mongols brought horses to the capital, private purchase by merchants was forbidden; clerks and runners who bought privately were punished.

sentences.zh: 康熙七年，裁茶馬御史，以馬政歸甘肅巡撫。

translations.literal: In Kangxi 7 the tea-horse censor was abolished and horse administration was assigned to the Gansu governor.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 7 the tea-horse censor was abolished and horse administration transferred to the Gansu governor.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，諭遣師中等往蒙古諸旗購馬，歸化城、科爾沁各二千匹，餘定額有差。

translations.literal: In year 34 it was ordered to send Shi Zhong and others to purchase horses from Mongol banners: two thousand each from Guihua City and Horqin, with fixed quotas varying for the rest.
translations.idiomatic: In year 34 the court dispatched Shi Zhong and others to purchase horses from Mongol banners—two thousand each from Guihua City and Horqin, with varying fixed quotas elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十二年，禁朝鮮買馬。

translations.literal: In Qianlong 12 Korea was forbidden to buy horses.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 12 Korea was forbidden to purchase horses.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，敕烏魯木齊市易哈薩克馬百三十餘匹歸巴里坤。

translations.literal: In year 25 it was ordered that more than one hundred thirty Kazakh horses traded at Urumqi be sent to Barkul.
translations.idiomatic: In year 25 over one hundred thirty Kazakh horses traded at Urumqi were ordered sent to Barkul.

sentences.zh: 旋以五吉等言，選哈薩克所易馬撥往巴里坤，遂停購買。

translations.literal: Soon, following Wuji and others' statement, selected Kazakh traded horses were allocated to Barkul and purchases were then halted.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, at Wuji and others' recommendation, selected Kazakh traded horses were allocated to Barkul and purchases were discontinued.

sentences.zh: 阿桂言伊犁易來哈薩克馬漸成大群，敕書嘉予。

translations.literal: Agui reported that Kazakh horses traded at Ili were gradually forming large herds; an edict praised and rewarded this.
translations.idiomatic: Agui reported that Kazakh horses traded at Ili were forming large herds; the emperor issued a commendatory edict.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，定江寧、浙江、福建駐防馬匹出口採買例。

translations.literal: In year 28 regulations were fixed for garrison horses of Jiangning, Zhejiang, and Fujian to be purchased through export trade.
translations.idiomatic: In year 28 the court fixed regulations for Jiangning, Zhejiang, and Fujian garrisons to procure horses through export purchase.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，以伊犁易哈薩克馬累積至多，擇巴里坤善地牧放。

translations.literal: In year 32, as Kazakh horses traded at Ili had accumulated greatly, good pasture at Barkul was selected for grazing.
translations.idiomatic: In year 32, as Kazakh horses traded at Ili had accumulated in large numbers, suitable pasture at Barkul was selected for grazing.

sentences.zh: 尋烏里雅蘇台馬缺，亦以哈薩克馬換易之。

translations.literal: Soon Uliastai had a horse shortage and Kazakh horses were also exchanged to fill it.
translations.idiomatic: When Uliastai faced a horse shortage, Kazakh horses were exchanged to replenish it as well.

sentences.zh: 陝、甘營馬，例調自伊犁轉補，道遠耗時。

translations.literal: Shaanxi and Gansu garrison horses were routinely transferred for replenishment from Ili—a distant route consuming much time.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi and Gansu garrison horses were routinely replenished from Ili—a distant route that consumed much time.

sentences.zh: 咸豐四年，用賡福請，由伊犁、塔爾巴哈台隨地變價，令各營自購。

translations.literal: In Xianfeng 4, following Yong Fu's request, horses at Ili and Tarbagatai were sold locally at market price and each garrison ordered to purchase its own.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 4, at Yong Fu's request, horses at Ili and Tarbagatai were sold locally at market price and each garrison ordered to purchase its own.

sentences.zh: 七年，並敕山東缺額馬，亦就近買補雲。

translations.literal: In year 7 it was also ordered that Shandong's shortfall in allotted horses be purchased and replenished nearby.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 Shandong's shortfall in allotted horses was likewise ordered replenished through local purchase.

sentences.zh: 貢馬昉於國初，歸化城土默特二旗，每歲四時貢馬百匹。

translations.literal: Tribute horses began at the founding of the state; the two Tumet banners of Guihua City presented one hundred horses each of the four seasons annually.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute horses date to the dynasty's founding; the two Tumet banners of Guihua City presented one hundred horses quarterly each year.

sentences.zh: 順治十三年，吐魯番貢三百二十四匹，嗣減令貢西馬四匹，蒙古馬十匹。

translations.literal: In Shunzhi 13 Turfan presented three hundred twenty-four horses; later this was reduced to four Western horses and ten Mongol horses.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 13 Turfan presented three hundred twenty-four horses; this was later reduced to four Western horses and ten Mongol horses annually.

sentences.zh: 康熙八年，以邊外蒙古貢馬，沿途抑買，諭嚴禁之。

translations.literal: In Kangxi 8, because frontier Mongols presenting tribute horses were forcibly bought out along the route, a stern prohibition was issued.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 8, as frontier Mongols presenting tribute horses faced forced purchase along the route, the court issued a strict prohibition.

sentences.zh: 三十年，諭土謝圖、車臣俱留汗號，貢白駝一、白馬八如初，自餘毋以九白進。

translations.literal: In year 30 it was ordered that Tushiyetu and Chechen retain their khan titles, presenting one white camel and eight white horses as before, but no longer presenting the nine whites beyond this.
translations.idiomatic: In year 30 Tushiyetu and Chechen were confirmed in their khan titles and directed to present one white camel and eight white horses as before, without the additional nine whites.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，喀爾喀蒙古獻駝馬，多不可計，感聖祖破噶爾丹，得歸原牧地也。

translations.literal: In year 35 Khalkha Mongols presented camels and horses beyond counting, grateful that the sage ancestor had defeated Galdan and they could return to their original pastures.
translations.idiomatic: In year 35 Khalkha Mongols presented camels and horses beyond counting, grateful that Kangxi had defeated Galdan and restored their original pastures.

sentences.zh: 四川各土司例貢及折徵馬，各營少者一、二匹，最多十二匹。

translations.literal: Sichuan native chiefs' routine tribute and commuted horses: each garrison received as few as one or two, at most twelve.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan chiefs' routine tribute and commuted horses ranged from one or two per garrison to a maximum of twelve.

sentences.zh: 甘肅唐古特七族西喇古兒例貢馬匹，各營最多者八十二匹，少者遞減至二、三匹。

translations.literal: Gansu's seven Tangut tribes of Xilagu'er routinely presented horses; each garrison received at most eighty-two, with reductions down to two or three.
translations.idiomatic: Gansu's seven Tangut Xilagu'er tribes routinely presented horses; garrisons received at most eighty-two, scaled down to two or three.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，諭四川土司折價馬每匹納銀十二兩，通省營馬改從驛馬例，納銀八兩，永著為令。

translations.literal: In Qianlong 1 it was ordered that Sichuan chiefs' commuted horses pay twelve taels of silver per horse, and province-wide garrison horses follow the courier-horse precedent at eight taels—permanently established as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 1 Sichuan chiefs' commuted horses were fixed at twelve taels of silver per head, and province-wide garrison horses at eight taels following courier-horse precedent—permanently established as law.

sentences.zh: 三十年，哈薩克沁德穆爾等獻馬。

translations.literal: In year 30 Kazakh chief Demur and others presented horses.
translations.idiomatic: In year 30 Kazakh chief Demur and others presented horses.

sentences.zh: 敕其餘馬赴伊犁，毋於喀什噶爾諸地貿易。

translations.literal: The remaining horses were ordered sent to Ili, not traded at Kashgar and other places.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining horses were ordered sent to Ili, not traded at Kashgar or elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 尋令沙拉伯爾游牧之哈薩克，與沙拉伯爾一體貢馬。

translations.literal: Soon Kazakhs pasturing at Shalabuer were ordered to present tribute horses together with Shalabuer as one.
translations.idiomatic: Kazakhs pasturing at Shalabuer were soon required to present tribute horses jointly with Shalabuer.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，停葉爾羌進馬。

translations.literal: In Jiaqing 1 presentation of horses from Yarkand was halted.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 1 horse presentations from Yarkand were discontinued.

sentences.zh: 十六年，諭烏里雅蘇台將軍等貢馬及備用馬選取之。

translations.literal: In year 16 it was ordered that the Uliastai general and others select from presented tribute horses and reserve horses.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16 the Uliastai general and others were directed to select from presented tribute and reserve horses.

sentences.zh: 又諭伊犁進馬，材具佶閒，足供御用，令正備貢各五匹，有私帶者，以違制論。

translations.literal: It was further ordered that Ili's presented horses, of excellent quality and sufficient for imperial use, be fixed at five each for regular and reserve tribute; private additions would be judged for violating regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Ili's presented horses, being of excellent quality fit for imperial use, were fixed at five each for regular and reserve tribute; private additions would be prosecuted as violations.

sentences.zh: 道光二年，從那彥成奏，青海屬玉樹番族歲納貢馬，據丁口數，依二十壯丁貢馬一匹例，按數遞裁。

translations.literal: In Daoguang 2, following Nayancheng's memorial, Yushu native tribes under Qinghai's annual tribute horses were, according to population, reduced stepwise under the precedent of one horse per twenty adult males.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 2, at Nayancheng's recommendation, Yushu native tribes under Qinghai had their annual tribute horses reduced stepwise under the rule of one horse per twenty adult males.

sentences.zh: 涼州屬番族歲仍納馬一匹。

translations.literal: Native tribes under Liangzhou still presented one horse annually.
translations.idiomatic: Native tribes under Liangzhou still presented one horse annually.

sentences.zh: 初內外蒙部多貴戚，每征伐，爭先輸馬、駝，漢、唐以來所未有也。

translations.literal: Early on inner and outer Mongol departments had many nobles; on each campaign they vied to present horses and camels first—unprecedented since Han and Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Early on Mongol nobles across inner and outer banners, on every campaign, vied to present horses and camels—a zeal unmatched since Han and Tang times.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，察哈爾親王、郡王、貝勒等，聞三籓叛，各獻馬匹佐軍。

translations.literal: Early in Kangxi, Chahar princes, commandery princes, beiles, and the like, hearing of the Three Feudatories' rebellion, each presented horses to assist the army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kangxi, upon news of the Three Feudatories' rebellion, Chahar princes, commandery princes, and beiles each presented horses to support the army.

sentences.zh: 道光九年，章佳胡圖克圖捐馬百匹，收其半。

translations.literal: In Daoguang 9 the Zhangjia Khutuktu donated one hundred horses; half were accepted.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 9 the Zhangjia Khutuktu donated one hundred horses; the court accepted half.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，察哈爾蒙旗捐馬千九百七十匹。

translations.literal: In year 23 Chahar Mongol banners donated one thousand nine hundred seventy horses.
translations.idiomatic: In year 23 Chahar Mongol banners donated one thousand nine hundred seventy horses.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，哲布尊丹巴等捐馬千匹，喀爾喀土謝圖等二千匹，錫林果勒盟長等三千匹，帝以其多，卻之。

translations.literal: Early in Xianfeng, Jebzundamba and others donated one thousand horses, Khalkha Tushiyetu and others two thousand, Xilin Gol league chiefs three thousand; the emperor, finding them excessive, declined them.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianfeng, Jebzundamba donated one thousand horses, Khalkha Tushiyetu two thousand, and Xilin Gol league chiefs three thousand; deeming the numbers excessive, the emperor declined them.

sentences.zh: 嗣聞已在途中，令擇善地牧以待用。

translations.literal: Later hearing they were already en route, he ordered good pasture selected to keep them until needed.
translations.idiomatic: Learning they were already en route, he ordered them pastured at a suitable location pending use.

sentences.zh: 自是三音諾顏部等，以軍事輸馬、駝，旋捐馬二千一百，錫林果勒盟等千二百，或留或否。

translations.literal: From then on the Setsen Khan department and others presented horses and camels for military affairs; soon two thousand one hundred horses were donated, Xilin Gol League one thousand two hundred—some retained, some not.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the Setsen Khan department and others presented horses and camels for military service; soon two thousand one hundred horses were donated and Xilin Gol League one thousand two hundred—some accepted, some declined.

sentences.zh: 七年，各部落蒙古王等捐馬六千四百匹，詔納之。

translations.literal: In year 7 Mongol princes of various tribes donated six thousand four hundred horses; an edict accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 Mongol princes of various tribes donated six thousand four hundred horses; the court accepted them by edict.

sentences.zh: 時粵、捻擾畿東，利於用騎也。

translations.literal: At the time the Cantonese and Nian rebels disturbed the capital region—cavalry was advantageous.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Cantonese and Nian rebels were ravaging the capital region, making cavalry especially valuable.

sentences.zh: 同治間，黑龍江將軍德英於呼倫貝爾各城勸捐軍馬。

translations.literal: During Tongzhi, Heilongjiang General Deying urged donation of military horses at various cities of Hulunbuir.
translations.idiomatic: During Tongzhi, Heilongjiang General Deying urged military horse donations across the cities of Hulunbuir.

sentences.zh: 光緒初，豐紳托克湍辦海防，時昭烏達盟郡王捐馬六百匹，因請踵行推廣勸諭，以助軍實雲。

translations.literal: Early in Guangxu, Fengshentuoketuan managed coastal defense; then a prince of Zhaowuda League donated six hundred horses, and he requested to follow with widespread exhortation to aid military strength.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guangxu, Fengshentuoketuan managed coastal defense; when a Zhaowuda League prince donated six hundred horses, he requested a broader campaign of exhortation to bolster military resources.

sentences.zh: 驛置肇自前漢，歷代因之。

translations.literal: Courier stations originated in Former Han and were continued by successive dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Courier stations originated in the Former Han and were maintained by successive dynasties.

sentences.zh: 清沿明制，設驛馬，為額四萬三千三百有奇。

translations.literal: The Qing followed the Ming system, establishing courier horses with a quota of more than forty-three thousand three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing followed the Ming system, establishing courier horses with a quota exceeding forty-three thousand three hundred.

sentences.zh: 各省驛制，定於康熙二年，凡齎奏官驛馬之數，各籓馬五匹，公、將軍、提督、督、撫三匹，總兵、巡鹽御史二匹，從兵部侍郎石麟請也。

translations.literal: Each province's courier system was fixed in Kangxi 2: for memorial-bearing officials, princes of the blood five horses, dukes, generals, provincial commanders, governors, and governors-general three, regional commanders and salt censors two—following Vice Minister of War Shi Lin's request.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial courier regulations were fixed in Kangxi 2: memorial-bearing officials received five horses for imperial clansmen, three for dukes, generals, provincial commanders, governors, and governors-general, and two for regional commanders and salt censors—at Vice Minister of War Shi Lin's request.

sentences.zh: 邊外之驛，定於九年，凡明詔特遣，及理籓院飭赴蒙古諸部宣諭公務，得乘邊外驛馬。

translations.literal: Frontier courier stations were fixed in year 9: for imperial edicts specially dispatched and Court of Colonial Affairs missions to Mongol banners for proclamation, frontier courier horses could be used.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier courier stations were fixed in year 9: imperial envoys on special commission and Court of Colonial Affairs missions proclaiming edicts in Mongol banners were entitled to frontier courier mounts.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，征噶爾丹，設邊外五處驛站，用便車糧運輸。

translations.literal: In year 35, campaigning against Galdan, five frontier courier stations were set up to facilitate transport of carts, grain, and supplies.
translations.idiomatic: In year 35, during the campaign against Galdan, five frontier courier stations were established to facilitate transport of carts, grain, and supplies.

sentences.zh: 又從理籓院言，自張家口外設蒙古驛。

translations.literal: Following the Court of Colonial Affairs' statement, Mongol courier stations were also set up beyond Zhangjiakou.
translations.idiomatic: At the Court of Colonial Affairs' recommendation, Mongol courier stations were also established beyond Zhangjiakou.

sentences.zh: 其大略也。

translations.literal: This was the general outline.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the general arrangement.

sentences.zh: 驛傳在僻地者，僅供本州縣所需，亦曰遞馬，額不過數匹。

translations.literal: Courier posts in remote places supplied only local prefecture and county needs, also called relay horses, with quotas of no more than a few.
translations.idiomatic: Courier posts in remote areas supplied only local prefectural and county needs, also termed relay horses, with quotas of only a few head.

sentences.zh: 沖繁州縣，置驛或二或三，額馬至六七十匹。

translations.literal: In busy prefectures and counties, two or three courier stations were set up, with quotas reaching sixty or seventy horses.
translations.idiomatic: In busy prefectures and counties, two or three courier stations were established, with quotas reaching sixty or seventy horses.

sentences.zh: 驛差大者，皇華使臣，朝貢蕃客，餘如大臣入覲、蒞官、視鹺、監稅皆是。

translations.literal: Major courier assignments included imperial envoys and tributary foreign guests; others such as grand ministers entering audience, taking office, inspecting salt, and supervising taxes were all included.
translations.idiomatic: Major courier assignments included imperial envoys and tributary foreign guests, as well as grand ministers attending audience, taking office, inspecting salt, and supervising taxes.

sentences.zh: 若齎奏員役，呈奉表冊，其小者也。

translations.literal: Memorial-bearing clerks and runners presenting memorials and registers were the minor assignments.
translations.idiomatic: Memorial-bearing clerks and runners presenting documents were minor assignments.

sentences.zh: 要者，如星馳飛遞，刻期立赴之屬。

translations.literal: Urgent ones were like star-rush flying dispatch, arriving within a set deadline.
translations.idiomatic: Urgent dispatches were those requiring star-rush delivery within a fixed deadline.

sentences.zh: 若閔勞恤死，允給郵傳，其散者也。

translations.literal: Condolences for the dead and consolation for the living, granted courier service, were the miscellaneous ones.
translations.idiomatic: Condolence missions and similar occasional assignments were miscellaneous uses of the courier service.

sentences.zh: 驛政弊壞，張汧嘗極言之。

translations.literal: The corruption of courier administration Zhang Qian once spoke of at length.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qian once spoke at length of the corruption plaguing courier administration.

sentences.zh: 越數誅求，橫索滋擾，蠹國病民，勢所必至。

translations.literal: Excessive exactions beyond quota, arbitrary demands and growing harassment, harming the state and afflicting the people—this was inevitable.
translations.idiomatic: Excessive exactions beyond quota, arbitrary demands, and growing harassment were inevitable—harming the state and afflicting the people.

sentences.zh: 已定例諸驛額馬，每年十踣其三，循例買補。

translations.literal: For allotted courier horses at established stations, three in ten died annually; replacements were purchased according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: For allotted courier horses at established stations, three in ten died annually and were replaced by regulation.

sentences.zh: 咸豐中，粵氛孔熾，湖、湘境為賊據，劫失驛騎，焚毀號舍，往往有之。

translations.literal: During Xianfeng, Cantonese rebels burned fiercely; Hunan and Hubei territories were seized by bandits; courier mounts were robbed and station buildings burned—this often occurred.
translations.idiomatic: During Xianfeng, as Cantonese rebels ravaged the realm and bandits seized Hunan and Hubei, courier mounts were robbed and station buildings burned with distressing frequency.

sentences.zh: 各州縣或買馬填補，或賃馬應差，其有失驛未設，即雇夫代馬。

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties either bought horses to fill gaps or hired horses for assignments; where stations were lost and not re-established, laborers were hired in place of horses.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and counties either purchased horses to fill gaps or hired mounts for assignments; where stations were lost, laborers were hired in place of horses.

sentences.zh: 甘肅舊設馬額六千餘，亦以軍興廢弛。

translations.literal: Gansu's former horse quota of more than six thousand also lapsed with the outbreak of war.
translations.idiomatic: Gansu's former quota of over six thousand horses also lapsed with the outbreak of war.

sentences.zh: 光緒九年，軍務既平，驛遞漸簡，所留馬視前減三分二，而驛政亦無所妨。

translations.literal: In Guangxu 9, with military affairs settled, courier dispatch was gradually simplified; retained horses were reduced by two-thirds from before, yet courier administration was unimpeded.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 9, with military affairs settled, courier dispatch was simplified; retained horses were cut by two-thirds, yet courier administration functioned without impediment.

sentences.zh: 十一年，新疆南路設驛。

translations.literal: In year 11 courier stations were set up on the southern route of Xinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 courier stations were established on Xinjiang's southern route.

sentences.zh: 是時，綜通國驛站歲費，約三百萬餘金。

translations.literal: At that time, totaling the empire's annual courier-station expenses, it came to about three million in cash.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the empire's annual courier-station expenses totaled roughly three million taels.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，劉坤一、張之洞條陳新法，謂驛站耗財，不如仿外人之郵政。

translations.literal: In year 29 Liu Kunyi and Zhang Zhidong memorialized on new methods, stating that courier stations wasted funds and it would be better to imitate foreign postal systems.
translations.idiomatic: In year 29 Liu Kunyi and Zhang Zhidong memorialized on reforms, arguing that courier stations wasted funds and that foreign-style postal service would be preferable.

sentences.zh: 郵政遞信速，驛政文報遲。

translations.literal: Postal service delivered letters swiftly; courier administration for documents was slow.
translations.idiomatic: Postal service delivered letters swiftly; courier administration for official documents was slow.

sentences.zh: 弊由有驛州縣馬缺額，又復疲瘦，驛丁或倚為利藪，因致稽延。

translations.literal: The abuse arose because counties with courier stations had shortfalls in allotted horses, which were also emaciated; courier runners sometimes treated this as a source of profit, causing delays.
translations.idiomatic: The abuse arose because courier counties faced horse shortfalls and emaciated mounts; runners sometimes treated the system as a source of profit, causing delays.

sentences.zh: 請設驛政局，推行郵政，俾驛鋪經費專取給郵資，即三百萬歲耗可以省出矣。

translations.literal: They requested establishing a Courier Administration Bureau, promoting postal service, so that courier-station expenses would be supplied solely from postal fees—the three million annual expenditure could then be saved.
translations.idiomatic: They proposed establishing a Courier Administration Bureau to promote postal service, funding courier stations solely from postal fees and thereby saving the three million taels in annual expenditure.

sentences.zh: 時韙其言。

translations.literal: At the time his words were approved.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court approved their proposal.

sentences.zh: 已而驛馬漸裁，嗣是驛遂廢不用。

translations.literal: Soon courier horses were gradually cut; thereafter courier service was abandoned and unused.
translations.idiomatic: Courier horses were gradually cut back, and eventually the courier system was abandoned altogether.

sentences.zh: 順治初，建常盈庫，凡車駕司朋椿站銀，武庫司馬值，太僕寺馬價皆儲之。

translations.literal: Early in Shunzhi the Ever-Full Treasury was built; all silver for the Imperial Transport Office's carriage and relay expenses, the Armory's horse values, and the Court of the Imperial Stud's horse prices were stored there.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shunzhi the Ever-Full Treasury was established to hold funds for the Imperial Transport Office's carriage and relay expenses, the Armory's horse values, and the Court of the Imperial Stud's horse prices.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，改常盈庫儲歸戶部。

translations.literal: Early in Kangxi, Ever-Full Treasury reserves were transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kangxi Ever-Full Treasury reserves were transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十六年，敕雲南營馬除十踣其三按例應賠外，其逾額踣斃者免賠椿銀。

translations.literal: In Qianlong 16 it was ordered that for Yunnan garrison horses, beyond the three in ten required compensation by regulation, deaths exceeding quota were exempt from compensation silver.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 16 Yunnan garrison horses beyond the statutory three-in-ten mortality rate were exempted from compensation silver for excess deaths.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，定給留圈馬乾，每匹視綠營稍優異。

translations.literal: In year 27 fodder allowances for corral horses kept in reserve were fixed, each horse receiving slightly more than Green Standard troops.
translations.idiomatic: In year 27 fodder allowances for reserved corral horses were fixed at a rate slightly above that for Green Standard troops.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，又令雲南買補馬價，每匹減銀三兩。

translations.literal: In year 38 Yunnan's horse replacement purchase price was again ordered reduced by three taels of silver per horse.
translations.idiomatic: In year 38 Yunnan's horse replacement purchase price was reduced by three taels per head.

sentences.zh: 初馬乾歲費約四十四萬有奇。

translations.literal: Initially annual fodder expenses were about four hundred forty thousand odd.
translations.idiomatic: Initially annual fodder expenses totaled roughly four hundred forty thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 道光中，從載銓等言，裁八旗官拴馬半額，以節出之費補兵餉焉。

translations.literal: During Daoguang, following Zaiquan and others' statement, half the quota of Banner officials' tethered horses was cut, and the savings used to supplement troop pay.
translations.idiomatic: During Daoguang, at Zaiquan and others' recommendation, half the quota of Banner officials' tethered horses was cut, with the savings applied to troop pay.

sentences.zh: 清初定現任官得養馬，餘悉禁之。

translations.literal: Early Qing regulations allowed incumbent officials to keep horses; all others were forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Early Qing regulations permitted only incumbent officials to keep horses; all others were forbidden.

sentences.zh: 尋許武進士、武舉、兵丁、捕役養馬。

translations.literal: Soon military jinshi, military licentiates, soldiers, and constables were permitted to keep horses.
translations.idiomatic: Military jinshi, military licentiates, soldiers, and constables were soon permitted to keep horses as well.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，禁民人養馬。

translations.literal: In Kangxi 1 common people were forbidden to keep horses.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 1 commoners were forbidden to keep horses.

sentences.zh: 有私販馬匹，為人首告者，馬給首告之人。

translations.literal: If horses were privately traded and someone reported it, the horses were given to the informant.
translations.idiomatic: If horses were privately traded and reported, the horses were awarded to the informant.

sentences.zh: 其主有官職，予重罰。

translations.literal: If the owner held office, heavy punishment was imposed.
translations.idiomatic: If the owner held office, heavy punishment was imposed.

sentences.zh: 平民荷校鞭責。

translations.literal: Commoners were cangued and flogged.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners were cangued and flogged.

sentences.zh: 十年，令民人仍得養馬。

translations.literal: In year 10 common people were again permitted to keep horses.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10 commoners were again permitted to keep horses.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，定出廠馬、駝，或踐食田禾，或縱逸侵擾，兵鞭責，官罰俸有差。

translations.literal: In year 26 it was fixed that stud-farm horses and camels let out, whether trampling crops or running loose to harass, brought flogging for soldiers and graded salary penalties for officers.
translations.idiomatic: In year 26 regulations fixed that stud-farm horses and camels released to trample crops or run loose brought flogging for soldiers and graded salary penalties for officers.

sentences.zh: 其兵丁強人代牧，乃勒索擾累者，兵發刑部，官降調。

translations.literal: If soldiers forced others to herd for them and extorted or harassed, soldiers were sent to the Ministry of Justice and officers demoted or transferred.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers who forced others to herd for them and extorted or harassed were sent to the Ministry of Justice; officers were demoted or transferred.

sentences.zh: 凡牧馬斃，則驗其皮，踣斃例須賠抵，有一九、一七之罰。

translations.literal: Whenever pastured horses died, the hide was inspected; death required compensation by regulation, with penalties of one-ninth and one-seventh.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever pastured horses died, the hide was inspected; deaths required compensation at rates of one-ninth and one-seventh by regulation.

sentences.zh: 應取駒千匹者，以百匹為一分，百匹者以十匹為一分。

translations.literal: Where one thousand foals were due, one hundred formed a unit; where one hundred, ten formed a unit.
translations.idiomatic: Where one thousand foals were due, one hundred formed a unit; where one hundred, ten formed a unit.

sentences.zh: 雍正十三年，定馬、駝出廠時，毛齒皆有冊，回日覈驗，如疲瘠十不及三，免議，否則兵鞭責，官罰俸有差。

translations.literal: In Yongzheng 13 it was fixed that when horses and camels left the stud, coat and teeth were recorded in registers; on return they were verified—if fewer than three in ten were emaciated, no inquiry; otherwise soldiers were flogged and officers fined by grade.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 13 when horses and camels left the stud, coat and teeth were recorded; on return, if fewer than three in ten were emaciated no penalty applied, otherwise soldiers were flogged and officers fined by grade.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，禁牧丁等盜馬私售，及與人乘，峻其科罰。

translations.literal: Early in Qianlong, herd attendants' theft and private sale of horses, and lending them for others to ride, were forbidden with severe penalties.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianlong theft and private sale of horses by herd attendants, and lending mounts to others, were forbidden with severe penalties.

sentences.zh: 十六年，嚴牧馬減克料草之罪。

translations.literal: In year 16 the crime of reducing or withholding fodder for pastured horses was strictly punished.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16 withholding fodder from pastured horses was severely punished.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，官馬出青，每百匹准倒十匹，逾額勒其買補。

translations.literal: In year 28 when government horses went out to green pasture, ten deaths per hundred were permitted; beyond quota they were compelled to purchase replacements.
translations.idiomatic: In year 28 when government horses went to summer pasture, ten deaths per hundred were permitted; beyond that quota replacements had to be purchased.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十一年，行圍木蘭，查獲私販馬匹諸犯，重懲之。

translations.literal: In Jiaqing 11, during the Mulan hunting expedition, offenders in private horse trading were discovered and severely punished.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 11, during the Mulan hunting expedition, private horse traders were discovered and severely punished.

sentences.zh: 因諭：「我朝講武時巡，扈從均給官馬。

translations.literal: An edict therefore stated: 'Our dynasty emphasizes martial training and seasonal tours; the entourage are all issued government horses.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stated: 'Our dynasty emphasizes martial training and seasonal tours; the entourage are all issued government horses.

sentences.zh: 大臣祿入較優，給馬較少。

translations.literal: Grand ministers have more generous salaries and receive fewer horses.
translations.idiomatic: Grand ministers, with more generous salaries, receive fewer horses.

sentences.zh: 官員兵丁，視差務之繁簡，定馬數之多寡，少者一、二匹，多至五匹，事竣原馬還官。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers, according to the complexity of assignments, were allotted varying numbers of horses—from one or two to as many as five; when duties ended the original horses were returned to the government.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and soldiers received one to five horses according to assignment complexity; when duties ended the original horses were returned to the government.

sentences.zh: 如踣斃，呈驗耳尾，仍按價折交。

translations.literal: If a horse died, ears and tail were presented for verification and compensation paid at the set price.
translations.idiomatic: If a horse died, ears and tail were presented for verification and compensation paid at the set price.

sentences.zh: 收放時，命王大臣督察。

translations.literal: When collecting and releasing horses, princes and grand ministers were ordered to supervise.
translations.idiomatic: When horses were collected and released, princes and grand ministers were ordered to supervise.

sentences.zh: 乃官兵等竟私鬻官單，察哈爾官兵收馬利，其折銀易於買補。

translations.literal: Yet officers and soldiers actually sold official requisition slips privately; Chahar officers and soldiers profited from receiving horses, as the converted silver was easier for buying replacements.
translations.idiomatic: Yet officers and soldiers privately sold official requisition slips; Chahar troops profited from receiving horses, as silver compensation was easier than buying replacements.

sentences.zh: 積弊日深，大妨馬政。

translations.literal: Accumulated abuses grew daily, greatly obstructing horse administration.
translations.idiomatic: Accumulated abuses deepened daily, gravely obstructing horse administration.

sentences.zh: 自後設有賣單及折收者，一體科罰。

translations.literal: Henceforth anyone selling slips or accepting cash conversion would be punished alike.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth anyone selling requisition slips or accepting cash conversion would be punished alike.

sentences.zh: 私買之馬販，從嚴問擬。

translations.literal: Horse dealers who bought privately would be prosecuted severely.
translations.idiomatic: Horse dealers who bought privately would be prosecuted severely.

sentences.zh: 大臣等其妥議定章以聞。

translations.literal: Grand ministers should properly deliberate and fix regulations to report.'
translations.idiomatic: Grand ministers are to deliberate and submit regulations for approval.'

sentences.zh: 」凡營馬或走脫竊失，責令賠補，謂之賠椿，年遞減十之一，至十年悉免之。

translations.literal: Whenever garrison horses escaped or were stolen, compensation was required—called compensation silver—reduced by one-tenth each year until fully exempt after ten years.
translations.idiomatic: When garrison horses escaped or were stolen, compensation was required—termed compensation silver—reduced by one-tenth annually until fully exempt after ten years.

sentences.zh: 應敵傷損者免賠。

translations.literal: Those wounded or damaged in battle were exempt from compensation.
translations.idiomatic: Horses wounded or damaged in battle were exempt from compensation.

sentences.zh: 騎至三年踣斃者亦免。

translations.literal: Those ridden for three years before dying were also exempt.
translations.idiomatic: Horses ridden for three years before dying were also exempt.

sentences.zh: 其餘一年或二三年內踣斃，賠額視其省而異，以十金為最多。

translations.literal: For the rest, dying within one or two or three years, compensation varied by province, with ten in gold as the maximum.
translations.idiomatic: For deaths within one to three years, compensation varied by province, with a maximum of ten taels of gold.

sentences.zh: 同治二年，定古北口盤獲私馬逾三十匹者送京，不及三十匹賞與兵丁，著為令。

translations.literal: In Tongzhi 2 it was fixed that private horses seized at Gubeikou exceeding thirty head were sent to the capital; fewer than thirty were rewarded to soldiers—established as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 2 private horses seized at Gubeikou exceeding thirty head were sent to the capital; fewer than thirty were rewarded to soldiers—established as permanent regulation.
